title: The equation, the windows, and the question
learning_goal: Read the induction equation as the race in symbols; know kinematic versus dynamic and the ABC dynamo windows; see that the knob is a panel of knobs, that simulations are too costly to cover it, and what this film asks.
takeaway: A dynamo can switch on, off and on again, real dynamos depend on many knobs, and simulations cover only a handful of settings: we need something that fills the gaps, and respects the physics.
notes: The T4 chapter card plays in the 3.2-s lead-in of 03.1 (no separate scene id), without the staircase, which is planted in 03.7 (a faint tier-2 preview in 03.3). Predict beat: Q3 of the outline in 03.4 (hold 3.0 s), read PREDICT on screen to avoid a clash with the question-card numbers. Badges: PROVED for the induction equation (P3 Theorem 2.1), CONTEXT for textbook or published facts (03.2, 03.3, 03.5, 03.6), MEASURED for E3 (03.4), PLANNED for the staircase of the PhD plan (03.7, shown from 'map'), none on the recap and the question card. No external fact: every claim is on the site, so no web source is cited. The growth rate is s (never lambda; the site writes lambda in E3). Thresholds are rounded on the main layer (about 9, 17.5, about 27) and exact on the formula layer; no 48³ marker (X1.3). 03.5 keeps one boundary switch, no ± numbers on the main layer, no 44 (D19), 'iron' in words. 03.7 separates project context (lower-thirds) from the study's question (critique B1); the supervisors are named only on the disclaimer lower-third (D6). Data: 03.4 reads data/e3_growth.json and data/e3_modes.json (existing extractor outputs, CONTRACT §5); 03.8 and ch03.Q read data/e3_growth.json for faithful thumbnails; no new data file is needed. The question card is numbered n = 4 on the assumption of one card per chapter in order (ch00.Q = 1, ch01.Q = 2, ch02.Q = 3): the consistency editor may renumber. Words budgeted at about 127.5 effective words per minute against target_s; estimates use the assembler formula (146 raw words per minute, 0.9 s per paragraph break, holds, lead-in and tail). Reviewed adversarially on 2026-11-08: changes and evidence in script/_review/ch03.md.

scenes.title: The induction equation, term by term

chapter.title: The equation, the windows, and the question

sentences.text: In the last chapter, the race was a picture: the {u}flow{/} stretches the field, and diffusion smudges it.
Physicists write the very same race as a single equation.
On the left: how fast the {b}magnetic field{/} changes, at each point.
First term on the right: the flow carries the field along and stretches it, like the threads.
Second term: diffusion smudges it, at a pace set by the magnetic diffusivity.
A poor conductor smudges fast.
Stretching against smudging: the whole race, in one line.

scenes.title: A conveyor belt that does not feel its cargo

params.note: illustrative curve only: no number is shown on screen (SCHEMATIC)

sentences.text: Picture the {u}flow{/} as a conveyor belt that does not feel its cargo.
A weak {b}field{/} rides on the imposed flow, and fades or grows exponentially.
On a log scale: a straight line, whose slope is the growth rate.
But a strong field pushes back on the flow, as it braked the copper disc: the line bends into a plateau.
These are the kinematic and dynamic regimes.
Flips live on the plateau.

labels: the field pushes back on the flow

formulas.tex: \text{kinematic: } \U \text{ imposed, } \partial_t\B = \nabla\times(\U\times\B) + \etaP\nabla^{2}\B \text{ is linear in } \B:\quad \B(\mathbf{x},t) = e^{s t}\,\hat{\B}(\mathbf{x}),\ \ s = \text{real growth rate (modes may also oscillate)}
\text{dynamic: the Lorentz force of } \B \text{ acts back on } \U \text{ and saturates the growth}

scenes.title: Twisting rooms: the ABC flow

sentences.text: To test ideas, physicists need a {u}flow{/} simple enough to write on one line, yet able to make a dynamo.
One classic choice: the ABC flow.
It fills space with identical twisting rooms.
Three crossed winds make the fluid corkscrew: it spins around the direction it moves.
This box returns higher on our climb.

labels: $\U = (A\sin z + C\cos y,\ B\sin x + A\cos z,\ C\sin y + B\cos x)$
$\nabla\times\U = \U$ · it spins around its own direction of motion

formulas.tex: \nabla\times\U = \U \ \ (\text{Beltrami flow, maximal helicity; streamlines partly chaotic}),\qquad \text{periodic box } [0, 2\pi)^3,\ \ A = B = C = 1

On 'abc-0.15': the letters A, B and C pulse once each (0.4 s, left to right) and the plain chip 'A = B = C = 1' appears at the right end of the line. scenes.title: Predict: once on, always on?

params.series: s, 32³ (fit on the second half of each run)

sentences.text: Now turn one {param}knob{/} on this flow: Rm. Turning it up means less diffusion.
Less smudging should only help the stretching.
So once the dynamo switches on, it stays on. Right?
Here is the growth rate, computed at twenty-four settings.
Below about nine, every {b}field{/} fades. Then growth turns positive: the dynamo is on.
Near seventeen and a half, it switches off again.
Above about twenty-seven, it comes back.
Not one threshold, but windows: turning a knob further does not always help.
It agrees with published results. No machine learning yet: this only tests the solver.

labels: dominant mode · |B| on the slice z = 0

scenes.title: A panel of knobs

sentences.text: Real dynamos have not one {param}knob{/}, but a panel.
How hard the metal is stirred; how well it conducts.
What the discs are made of: remember the iron.
How unequal their speeds are: that is when VKS flipped.
For DRESDYN, a precessing tank: how fast its axis turns.
Even the wall counts: in VKS simulations, changing only its magnetic condition raised the threshold by about forty percent.

scenes.visual: Render class flat. On 'panel-0.15': the single green knob left at the end of 03.4 (label 'Rm') slides to the centre, then splits (T1 morph, 1.4 s) into a row of five green knobs (M2, Kit.knob x 5, about 220 px apart, y 300-520), each named in words under it from params.knobs (Inter 32 px, name on line 1, gloss on line 2): 'Re · stirring', 'Rm · stretch vs smudge', 'iron · disc material', 'asymmetry · unequal disc speeds' (ch02 narrates the VKS impellers as 'bladed discs' and labels them 'disc 1', 'disc 2' in 02.6), 'precession · the tank's axis turns'. Words only: 'iron', never mu_r (symbol sheet D3); no numbers on the knobs. All five start dim (40 %); each lights to 100 % on its cue and its pointer turns a little (Scene.spring, at most 3 % overshoot). On 'stir-0.15': Re and Rm light. On 'iron-0.15': the iron knob lights; above it a small grey impeller icon swaps from light grey (steel) to dark grey (soft iron), a callback to 02.5. On 'asym-0.15': the asymmetry knob lights; above it two small grey impellers spin at visibly different speeds and a tiny polarity strip (two vermillion shades) flips once, a callback to 02.6. On 'prec-0.15': the precession knob lights; above it a small grey cylinder spins while its axis slowly turns, dashed outline (DRESDYN is under way). On 'wall-0.15': the knob row shrinks up to y 140-300 (icons fade); below it a toggle switch 'wall condition' (left, x about 300, y 560; positions 'simplified' and 'vacuum') and a short green axis 'Rm' (x 600-1600, y 600, no tick numbers) with a threshold marker and a vermillion-tinted region to its right labelled 'dynamo'. At params.wall_switch.flip_at the switch flips (detent sfx) and the marker slides right by the ratio threshold_shift.to / threshold_shift.from (1.2 s, cubic), the vermillion region shrinking with it; label 'boundary condition: threshold +40 % (simulations)'. The three definitions of Rm are not here (they live in X6.0), and 44 is never shown (D19). Badge CONTEXT top-right. Formula layer from 'wall', label 'Formula · R:143'. scenes.title: A handful of dots

sentences.text: Every turbulent dynamo simulation in three dimensions is very costly.
So only a handful of knob settings get simulated.
Each one is a mountain of data: a single snapshot can weigh more than a gigabyte.
Each run holds only a few flips.
And between the dots, there is nothing at all.

sentences.text: Those gaps are where this film lives.
The study behind this film asks three things.
One: can a {model}machine{/} learn the whole family of fields, even at knob settings between the dots?
Two: can it respect each law where it holds, exactly in every field, or {metric}on average{/} over many fields?
Three: can it tell us {metric}how often{/} the field flips?
To find out, the study's plan climbs a staircase, from three numbers to the shapes of real experiments.
One honest note: this independent study is prospective, built on small experiments on an ordinary computer, and not endorsed by MilaDy, its partners or the supervisors.

question.en: With only a handful of runs, should the settings be *spread evenly*, or *packed* near each threshold?
question.fr: Avec une poignée de simulations, faut-il répartir les valeurs des paramètres régulièrement, ou les resserrer près de chaque seuil ?
question.why: Near a threshold the field changes fastest with the knob, and the PhD plan leaves the density of points there open.
question.unblocks: Rm values of the 64³ ABC sweep (integer steps for now) and Re values at each Pm of the Taylor–Green runs.
question.why_fr: Près d'un seuil, le champ change le plus vite avec le paramètre, et le plan de thèse laisse ouverte la densité de points à cet endroit.
question.unblocks_fr: Valeurs de Rm du balayage ABC en 64³ (pas entier pour l'instant) et valeurs de Re à chaque Pm des simulations Taylor–Green.
